items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: He used to borrow my records of contemporary composers, Cage and Morton Feldman and others, Stockhausen

ctx.x: Did you feel that his personality was reflected in his music that seemed to always be seeking the far boundaries? I may not be speaking exactly on point here but did he have a personality that reflected the way he played?

He had a conversation that reflected the way he played. His personality was that of one that you would recognize, a very, very, very smart person who had a mind that was flying all over the place as he talked, who was extremely curious about all manner of things and had strong opinions about all manner of things. He used to borrow my records of contemporary composers, Cage and Morton Feldman and others, Stockhausen — he would borrow those until I stopped lending them to him because he’d always give them back all…
Did you hear him with various sidemen and if so did you observe anything watching the sidemen that reflected the challenge of playing with Cecil Taylor?
